note: The run to Athens that gave the marathon its name.
The 300 – and many more Greeks than the films show.
Themistocles lures the Persian fleet into the straits.
Alexander breaks the Persian Empire.

title: Founding of Rome
description: According to legend, Romulus founds Rome on the Palatine Hill.
note: Legend, not history – but every Roman knew the date.
Hannibal's masterpiece of encirclement.
Scipio finally defeats Hannibal.
Octavian wins; the Republic becomes an Empire.

title: Colosseum opens
description: Emperor Titus inaugurates the Flavian Amphitheatre with 100 days of games.
note: Go early in the morning to avoid the queues.
Three legions lost; Rome stops at the Rhine.

title: Sack of Rome
description: The Visigoths under Alaric sack Rome for the first time in 800 years.

note: The last great battle between galleys.
Nelson's victory – and death.
Turning point of the Pacific War.

title: National Maritime Museum
description: Britain's national museum of seafaring in Greenwich.
note: Has a whole gallery on Trafalgar.

title: Landing in Sicily
description: Grandpa landed near Gela with his unit.
note: From his first letter home.

title: Battle of Monte Cassino
description: Months of fighting around the abbey.
note: He wrote that he could see the abbey from his trench.
His brother, uncle Joe, was on Omaha Beach.

title: Crossing the Rhine at Remagen
description: The bridge was still standing when they arrived.

title: Home again
description: Back in Milan for Christmas.
note: The last letter in the box.

title: Sagrada Família
description: Construction of Gaudí's basilica begins; it is still unfinished.
note: Book tickets online!

title: Night train to Lyon
description: Not historic, but unforgettable.

note: Saw the column at Place de la Bastille.

title: Charles Bridge
description: Charles IV lays the foundation stone of the bridge in Prague.
note: Best at sunrise.

title: Brandenburg Gate
description: Berlin's neoclassical gate, completed in 1791.

note: Walked along the East Side Gallery.
Pompeii and Herculaneum were buried.
London rebuilt in brick and stone.
Lisbon was rebuilt on a grid – the Pombaline style.

title: Z3, the first working programmable computer
description: Konrad Zuse's electromechanical Z3, built in Berlin-Kreuzberg from telephone relays, is the first working programmable, binary computer.

title: Colossus attacks its first message
description: The first programmable electronic digital computer starts breaking German Lorenz cipher traffic at Bletchley Park.

title: ENIAC is unveiled
description: The Moore School of Electrical Engineering in Philadelphia presents a room-sized general-purpose electronic computer.

title: The Manchester Baby runs the first stored program
description: The first program held in electronic memory runs at the University of Manchester.

title: Dartmouth workshop names 'artificial intelligence'
description: A summer gathering at Dartmouth College founds artificial intelligence as a research field.

title: First ARPANET message
description: A login attempt from UCLA to Stanford is the first message on the network that grew into the Internet.

title: Xerox Alto at PARC
description: Xerox PARC builds a personal computer with a mouse and windows years before they reach the market.

title: The Web is proposed at CERN
description: Tim Berners-Lee circulates 'Information Management: A Proposal' in a Swiss physics laboratory.

title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
description: A computer wins a six-game chess match against the reigning world champion in New York.

title: Geiger-Marsden gold foil experiment
description: Alpha particles bounce off thin gold foil in Manchester, and Rutherford infers the atomic nucleus.

title: Hahn and Strassmann split the uranium nucleus
description: At the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Chemistry in Berlin-Dahlem, barium turns up where none should be.

title: Chicago Pile-1 goes critical
description: Under the stands of a university football stadium, the first man-made nuclear reactor sustains a chain reaction.

title: B Reactor goes critical at Hanford
description: The first full-scale plutonium production reactor starts its chain reaction on the Columbia River.

title: Obninsk connects to the grid
description: The world's first nuclear power plant to feed an electric grid starts up near Moscow.

title: JET, Europe's fusion experiment
description: At Culham in England, the largest tokamak of its time produces its first plasma.

title: Higgs boson announced at CERN
description: ATLAS and CMS report a new particle matching the Higgs boson, found with the Large Hadron Collider.

title: Fusion ignition at the National Ignition Facility
description: Laser fusion produces more energy from the target than the lasers delivered to it.

title: Tycho Brahe builds Uraniborg
description: An island observatory in the Danish sound yields the most precise naked-eye star and planet measurements ever made.

title: Neptune is found where mathematics said
description: Johann Galle at the Berlin Observatory spots the planet within a degree of Le Verrier's prediction.

title: Hubble shows the universe is expanding
description: Edwin Hubble's measurements at Mount Wilson show galaxies receding in proportion to their distance.

title: Cosmic microwave background discovered
description: Penzias and Wilson cannot get rid of a hiss in their horn antenna in New Jersey: the afterglow of the Big Bang.

title: Lovell Telescope starts tracking
description: Jodrell Bank's giant dish tracks the rocket of Sputnik 1 within days of the first operation.

title: Jocelyn Bell finds the first pulsar
description: A regular radio pulse in the Cambridge antenna data leads to the discovery of neutron stars.

title: LIGO detects gravitational waves
description: The Hanford detector in Washington state, with its twin in Louisiana, records two black holes merging.

title: First image of a black hole
description: A network of radio dishes, including the ALMA array in the Atacama, images the shadow of M87*'s black hole.

title: Jenner's first smallpox vaccination
description: A country doctor in Berkeley inoculates a boy with cowpox and starts vaccination.

title: Ether anaesthesia demonstrated in public
description: In the operating theatre of Massachusetts General Hospital a patient has surgery without feeling pain.

title: Semmelweis introduces handwashing
description: In Vienna's maternity clinic, mortality from childbed fever falls when doctors wash their hands.

title: John Snow and the Broad Street pump
description: A Soho cholera outbreak is traced to one water pump, a founding case of epidemiology.

title: Pasteur treats the first rabies patient
description: Louis Pasteur vaccinates a bitten boy in Paris, and the institute that bears his name follows.

title: Fleming notices penicillin
description: A mould spoils a culture plate at St Mary's Hospital in Paddington, and the first antibiotic is found.

title: Banting's idea that led to insulin
description: In London, Ontario, a young surgeon sketches the experiment that leads to the use of insulin.

title: First human heart transplant
description: Christiaan Barnard's team in Cape Town replaces a patient's heart with a donor's.

title: Last natural case of smallpox
description: A hospital cook in Merca, Somalia, is the last person to catch smallpox in the wild.

title: Schliemann digs at Hisarlik
description: An amateur archaeologist starts excavating a mound in Turkey and finds layers of the legendary city.

title: Rosetta Stone found
description: French soldiers rebuilding a fort in Rashid find the stone that later unlocks Egyptian hieroglyphs.

title: Hiram Bingham reaches Machu Picchu
description: A Yale lecturer is led to the Inca citadel above the Urubamba valley, and publicises it.

title: Tutankhamun's tomb discovered
description: Howard Carter's team finds the first step to an almost intact royal tomb in the Valley of the Kings.

title: Lascaux cave found
description: Four teenagers and a dog find Paleolithic paintings in the Dordogne.

title: Dead Sea Scrolls discovered
description: A shepherd looking for a lost goat finds jars of ancient scrolls in caves near the Dead Sea.

title: Terracotta Army discovered
description: Farmers digging a well near Xi'an strike the army that guards the first emperor of China.

title: Ötzi found on the Tisenjoch
description: Hikers find a 5,300-year-old mummy in the melting ice of the Alps.

title: Göbekli Tepe excavations begin
description: Klaus Schmidt starts digging monumental pillars older than Stonehenge by 6,000 years.

title: Fram frozen into the Arctic ice
description: A ship built to be squeezed upward by pack ice starts its drift across the Arctic Ocean; pinned at Nansen's fix of 5 October 1893.

title: Gjøa winters at Gjoa Haven
description: Roald Amundsen's small sloop makes the first full transit of the Northwest Passage.

title: Belgica locked in the ice
description: A Belgian expedition is the first to spend a winter south of the Antarctic Circle, by accident.

title: Mawson winters at Cape Denison
description: The windiest place at sea level: the Australasian Antarctic Expedition's huts still stand.

title: Scott's hut at Cape Evans
description: The Terra Nova expedition's base on Ross Island, still standing and still full of its supplies.

title: Endurance crushed by the ice
description: Shackleton's ship sinks in the Weddell Sea; the wreck was found in 2022 at almost the same spot.

title: Coldest temperature ever measured
description: A Soviet research station in Antarctica records -89.2 °C.

title: Franklin's Erebus found
description: Canadian searchers find the flagship of the lost Franklin expedition. The exact site is not published; the pin is the centre of the protected area.

title: First public demonstration of the Mark I Perceptron
description: Frank Rosenblatt's Mark I Perceptron, a neural-network machine for image recognition built at the Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory in Buffalo, New York, was first demonstrated publicly on 23 June 1960.

title: Weizenbaum's ELIZA chatbot appears at MIT
description: Joseph Weizenbaum of MIT published ELIZA in Communications of the ACM. The program imitated a psychotherapist by matching keywords in typed input and answering with scripted replies.

title: Shakey, the first mobile robot that reasons about its actions
description: SRI's Artificial Intelligence Center in Menlo Park built Shakey, a wheeled robot combining perception, planning and navigation, with funding from DARPA.

title: IBM Watson wins Jeopardy! against human champions
description: IBM's Watson question-answering system played former Jeopardy! champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter in a televised match and won, with episodes aired 14-16 February 2011.

title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol 4-1 in Seoul
description: Google DeepMind's AlphaGo played Lee Sedol in a five-game Go match at the Four Seasons Hotel in Seoul and won 4-1, a first for a program against a top professional.

title: DARPA Urban Challenge for driverless cars
description: Autonomous vehicles drove a 96 km urban course with traffic at the former George Air Force Base in Victorville, California. Tartan Racing of Carnegie Mellon won.

title: Libratus beats four poker professionals in Pittsburgh
description: The Carnegie Mellon poker program Libratus played 120,000 hands of heads-up no-limit Texas hold'em against four professionals over 20 days and finished well ahead.

title: Chatbot Eugene Goostman is declared to pass a Turing test
description: At the Royal Society in London, the chatbot Eugene Goostman, posing as a 13-year-old Ukrainian boy, convinced 33 percent of judges it was human; the claim was widely disputed.

title: The Lighthill debate on AI at the Royal Institution
description: A televised debate on artificial intelligence was held at the Royal Institution in London after the critical Lighthill report, which helped cut British AI research funding.

title: Self-driving Uber test car kills a pedestrian in Tempe
description: A prototype Uber self-driving Volvo XC90 struck and killed Elaine Herzberg as she crossed Mill Avenue in Tempe, Arizona, the first pedestrian death involving such a vehicle.

title: DARPA Robotics Challenge finals at Fairplex
description: Humanoid and other robots attempted disaster-response tasks at the Fairplex in Pomona, California. Team KAIST's DRC-Hubo won the finals on completion time.

title: LeNet convolutional networks read handwritten digits at Bell Labs
description: At AT&T Bell Laboratories in Holmdel, Yann LeCun's group trained convolutional neural networks with backpropagation to read handwritten zip code digits.

title: Stanford AI Laboratory settles into the D.C. Power building
description: John McCarthy's Stanford AI Laboratory, founded in 1963, was housed from 1966 to 1979 in the D.C. Power building on a hill above Felt Lake, about 8 km from the main campus.

title: Basil Brown opens the Sutton Hoo ship burial
description: Self-taught archaeologist Basil Brown began excavating Mound 1 at Sutton Hoo for landowner Edith Pretty; Charles Phillips took over the burial chamber the following month.

title: Chauvet Cave rediscovered in the Ardeche
description: Speleologists Eliette Brunel-Deschamps, Christian Hillaire and Jean-Marie Chauvet entered a cave in the Ardeche gorge and found its Paleolithic wall paintings.

title: Mary Rose hull raised from the Solent
description: The surviving hull of Henry VIII's warship Mary Rose, sunk in 1545, was lifted from the seabed in the Solent by the Mary Rose Trust.

title: Richard III's skeleton unearthed under a Leicester car park
description: An archaeological dig on the site of the Greyfriars Priory found a skeleton later identified by the University of Leicester as Richard III, announced on 4 February 2013.

title: Sanz de Sautuola recognises the Altamira paintings
description: Amateur archaeologist Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola, led by his daughter Maria, recognised the markings on the Altamira cave walls as drawings.

title: Layard finds the Nineveh library tablets
description: Austen Henry Layard found the first cuneiform tablets of the library at Kouyunjik, the mound of ancient Nineveh, in the South-West Palace of Sennacherib.

title: Woolley begins excavating Ur
description: Leonard Woolley began excavations at Ur in 1922, funded by the British Museum and the University of Pennsylvania, continuing until 1934.

title: Herschel spots Uranus from a Bath garden
description: From the garden of his house at 19 New King Street, William Herschel observed an object he later showed to be a planet, Uranus, the first found with a telescope.

title: Hale Telescope first light at Palomar
description: The 200-inch Hale Telescope at Palomar Observatory made its first observation, directed by Edwin Hubble, of Hubble's Variable Nebula (NGC 2261).

title: Very Large Array is inaugurated in New Mexico
description: The radio telescope array of 27 dishes on the Plains of San Agustin was formally inaugurated in 1980, after its first antenna was installed in 1975.

title: South Pole Telescope sees first light
description: A 10-metre millimetre-wave telescope at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station made its first observations, to map the cosmic microwave background.

title: Arecibo message beamed toward M13
description: A short binary radio message was broadcast from the Arecibo Telescope in Puerto Rico toward a star cluster, at a ceremony marking the telescope's remodelling.

title: Keck I sees first light on Mauna Kea
description: The first of the two 10-metre Keck telescopes, then the largest optical telescope in the world, saw first light near the summit of Mauna Kea, Hawaii.

title: Mendel presents his pea-plant experiments in Brno
description: Gregor Mendel read his results on inheritance in pea plants to the Natural History Society of Brno; the experiments were done in the garden of St Thomas's Abbey.

title: Darwin moves into Down House
description: Charles Darwin moved his family to Down House in Kent, where he lived for the rest of his life and wrote On the Origin of Species.

title: Watson and Crick publish the DNA double helix
description: Watson and Crick's one-page Nature paper proposed the double-helix structure of DNA, worked out at the Cavendish Laboratory in Cambridge.

title: Franklin and Gosling take Photo 51 of DNA
description: At King's College London, Rosalind Franklin and Raymond Gosling produced Photo 51, an X-ray diffraction image of DNA that later helped establish its helical form.

title: Miller and Urey simulate early-Earth chemistry
description: Stanley Miller, working under Harold Urey, ran a sealed-flask experiment simulating early Earth conditions that produced amino acids from simple gases.

title: Dolly the sheep is born at the Roslin Institute
description: Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell, was born at the Roslin Institute near Edinburgh.

title: First test-tube baby is born in Oldham
description: Louise Brown, the first baby conceived by in vitro fertilisation, was born at Oldham and District General Hospital, now the Royal Oldham Hospital site.

title: Avery team identifies DNA as the genetic material
description: Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty showed at the Rockefeller Institute that DNA, not protein, carries the transforming principle in bacteria.

title: Hershey and Chase confirm DNA carries genes
description: Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase used radiolabelled bacteriophages to show that DNA is the genetic material of viruses.

title: Morgan's Fly Room: the white-eyed fruit fly
description: At Columbia University, Thomas Hunt Morgan's fruit-fly work found the white-eyed mutant and linked genes to chromosomes.

title: Asilomar conference on recombinant DNA
description: Scientists met at Asilomar on the Monterey Peninsula and drafted voluntary safety guidelines for recombinant DNA research.

title: Charles Darwin Research Station is established
description: A research station was established at Puerto Ayora in the Galapagos in 1959, the centenary of On the Origin of Species, for study and conservation.

title: Sanger Centre opens at Hinxton
description: The Sanger Centre opened on the Wellcome Genome Campus at Hinxton and became a leading sequencing centre of the Human Genome Project.

title: First transistor demonstrated at Bell Labs
description: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain at Bell Laboratories built the first working point-contact transistor in December 1947; the critical experiment was on 16 December.

title: First planar integrated circuit tested at Fairchild
description: A Fairchild Semiconductor team led by Jay Last tested the first operational planar, monolithic integrated circuit on 27 September 1960, using Robert Noyce's planar concept.

title: MOSFET demonstrated at Bell Labs
description: Mohamed Atalla and Dawon Kahng's team at Bell Labs demonstrated a working silicon MOS transistor in 1960, the device behind most modern chips.

title: One-transistor DRAM cell invented at IBM
description: Robert Dennard at the IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center invented the one-transistor, one-capacitor DRAM cell in 1966; the patent was granted in 1968.

title: IBM RAMAC, the first hard disk drive, announced
description: IBM announced the 350 Disk Storage Unit of the RAMAC 305 computer on 14 September 1956; it was developed at IBM's San Jose laboratory.

title: Gordon Moore publishes his law
description: Gordon Moore, director of research at Fairchild Semiconductor, published his observation about doubling chip components in Electronics magazine on 19 April 1965.

title: Intel 4004 microprocessor released
description: Intel's first advertisement for the 4004, an early commercial single-chip microprocessor designed by Federico Faggin, Ted Hoff and Stanley Mazor, ran on 15 November 1971.

title: Pentium FDIV bug reported to Intel
description: Mathematician Thomas Nicely of Lynchburg College reported a Pentium floating-point division error to Intel on 24 October 1994; Intel recalled the chips that December.

title: TSMC founded in Hsinchu
description: The Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company was founded on 21 February 1987 in Hsinchu, the first pure-play chip foundry, within the Industrial Technology Research Institute.

title: Earth Simulator opens in Yokohama
description: The Earth Simulator supercomputer opened at JAMSTEC's Yokohama Institute on 11 March 2002 and ranked first on the TOP500 list from June 2002 to 2004.

title: Sunway TaihuLight tops the TOP500
description: Sunway TaihuLight, at the National Supercomputing Center in Wuxi, became the world's fastest supercomputer on the TOP500 list in June 2016.

title: Roadrunner passes one petaflop
description: IBM's Roadrunner broke the one-petaflop barrier on 25 May 2008 on its fourth attempt, while still at IBM's Poughkeepsie site, before moving to Los Alamos.

title: Fugaku tops the TOP500
description: Fugaku, at the RIKEN Center for Computational Science in Kobe, became the world's fastest supercomputer on the June 2020 TOP500 list, displacing IBM's Summit.

title: Frontier reaches exascale at Oak Ridge
description: Frontier, hosted at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, measured 1.1 exaflops in May 2022 and topped the June 2022 TOP500 list.

title: IBM RAMAC, the first hard disk drive system, is announced
description: IBM announced the 305 RAMAC, whose disk storage was designed at its San Jose Research Laboratory at 99 Notre Dame Street.

title: LEO I runs the first routine business job at Lyons
description: At the J. Lyons company's Cadby Hall, the LEO computer ran its first business application, Bakery Valuations, costing ingredients for bread and cakes.

title: Steve Jobs unveils the Macintosh at the Flint Center
description: Apple's original Macintosh was introduced in January 1984 at a press conference in the Flint Center at De Anza College, Cupertino.

title: The Altair 8800 kit computer appears from MITS
description: MITS of Albuquerque, based at 6328 Linn NE, launched the Altair 8800 kit through the January 1975 Popular Electronics cover story.

title: Atanasoff-Berry Computer is tested at Iowa State
description: The ABC, an electronic digital calculator, was built in the basement of the physics building at Iowa State College in Ames and successfully tested in 1942.

title: EDSAC runs its first programs at Cambridge
description: EDSAC, built at the University of Cambridge Mathematical Laboratory, ran its first programs on 6 May 1949; the first computed a table of squares.

title: First Cray-1 supercomputer installed at Los Alamos
description: The first Cray-1 system, serial number 001, was installed at Los Alamos National Laboratory in 1976 for a six-month trial.

title: Whirlwind I computes interception courses at MIT
description: The Whirlwind I computer at MIT successfully computed interception courses on 20 April 1951.

title: UNIVAC I is accepted by the US Census Bureau
description: The first UNIVAC I, built at the Eckert-Mauchly factory at 3747 Ridge Avenue, Philadelphia, was accepted by the Census Bureau on 31 March 1951.

title: Keeling Curve begins at Mauna Loa
description: Charles David Keeling began continuous carbon dioxide measurements at Mauna Loa Observatory in March 1958, the start of the Keeling Curve record of rising atmospheric CO2.

title: Mauna Loa Observatory founded
description: The U.S. Weather Bureau founded Mauna Loa Observatory on the northern flank of the volcano at about 3,394 m to monitor the free atmosphere; it later joined NOAA's baseline network.

title: Ozone hole discovered from Halley Bay
description: Ozone measurements made at the British Antarctic Survey's Halley station led to the discovery of the Antarctic ozone hole in 1985. The station then stood on the Brunt Ice Shelf.

title: Trieste dives to the Challenger Deep
description: Jacques Piccard and Lt. Don Walsh took the bathyscaphe Trieste to the bottom of the Challenger Deep, the first crewed descent to the deepest known point of the ocean, about 10,900 m down.

title: Hydrothermal vents found by Alvin
description: Scientists in the submersible Alvin, including Jack Corliss and Tjeerd van Andel, observed and sampled hot vents and their animal communities on the Galapagos Rift, the first such discovery.

title: GRIP ice core drilled to bedrock
description: The European Greenland Ice Core Project drilled a 3,029 m core at Summit, reaching the base of the ice sheet in 1992 and giving a long record of past climate.

title: Camp Century built under the ice
description: The U.S. Army built Camp Century, a base inside the Greenland ice sheet, in 1959. It served as a research station and, as later revealed, a preliminary site for Project Iceworm.

title: Hawaiian Volcano Observatory begins
description: Geologist Thomas Jaggar began operating the Hawaiian Volcano Observatory at the rim of Kilauea in 1912, one of the first full-time volcano observatories.

title: Vesuvius Observatory founded
description: The Bourbon king Ferdinand II founded the Vesuvius Observatory in 1841 on the Colle del Salvatore, making it the world's oldest volcano observatory.

title: Mohorovicic discovers the Moho in Zagreb
description: Analysing seismograms of the Pokuplje earthquake of 8 October 1909 in Zagreb, Andrija Mohorovicic found the boundary between the Earth's crust and mantle.

title: Record 231 mph wind on Mount Washington
description: Observers at the summit weather station recorded a wind gust of 231 mph, the highest surface wind speed known at the time, a record that stood until 1996.

title: Kola Superdeep Borehole drilling starts
description: Soviet drillers began the Kola Superdeep Borehole in Murmansk Oblast. It reached 12,262 m in 1989 and remains the deepest human-made hole.

title: Drake strikes oil near Titusville
description: Edwin Drake's well in Pennsylvania reached 69.5 feet and struck oil, launching the modern petroleum industry in the United States.

title: Pearl Street Station powers lower Manhattan
description: Thomas Edison's central power station at 255-257 Pearl Street began generating electricity for customers in the Financial District of New York City.

title: Niagara Falls Adams power plant starts
description: The Edward Dean Adams Power Plant at Niagara Falls began operating in 1895; its transformer house is the only surviving structure.

title: First Edison hydroelectric station, Appleton
description: The Vulcan Street Plant on the Fox River began operating, the first Edison hydroelectric central station serving private and commercial customers in North America.

title: First geothermal power generator at Larderello
description: Prince Piero Ginori Conti tested the first geothermal power generator at the Larderello dry steam field in Italy, lighting a few light bulbs.

title: First megawatt wind turbine on Grandpa's Knob
description: The 1.25 MW Smith-Putnam turbine near Castleton, Vermont, was first synchronized to the local grid; it was the world's first megawatt-size wind turbine.

title: Lucas Gusher blows in at Spindletop
description: The Lucas Gusher at Spindletop near Beaumont, Texas, erupted over 150 feet high and flowed for nine days, starting the Texas oil boom.

title: Cragside hydroelectric power, Northumberland
description: William Armstrong installed a Siemens dynamo at Cragside in 1870, described as the world's first hydroelectric power station; it later lit his house.

title: World's first offshore wind farm, Vindeby
description: Eleven 450 kW turbines were commissioned off Vindeby on Lolland, Denmark, making the world's first offshore wind farm; it was removed in 2017.

title: Ivanpah solar power tower plant opens
description: The 392 MW Ivanpah concentrated solar plant, with three towers and 173,500 heliostats in the Mojave Desert, was formally opened.

title: DniproHES begins generating at Zaporizhzhia
description: The Dnieper Hydroelectric Station at Zaporizhzhia started producing electricity; the dam was destroyed in 1941 and rebuilt from 1944 to 1950.

title: PG&E geothermal plant starts at The Geysers
description: Pacific Gas and Electric began operating an 11 MW geothermal power plant at The Geysers in California, a field that had a small 250 kW plant in 1921.

title: Brooklyn Bridge opens across the East River
description: The Brooklyn Bridge, a hybrid cable-stayed and suspension bridge linking Manhattan and Brooklyn, opened to traffic in 1883 and was then the longest suspension bridge in the world.

title: Suez Canal opens to shipping
description: The Suez Canal, built by the Suez Canal Company, opened in 1869 and gave ships a direct sea route between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea without sailing round Africa.

title: Panama Canal opens with the SS Ancon transit
description: The Panama Canal was formally opened when the cargo ship SS Ancon made the first official transit, joining the Atlantic and Pacific oceans across the isthmus.

title: Eiffel Tower completed in Paris
description: The Eiffel Tower, a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars, was completed in 1889 as the entrance arch of the Exposition Universelle, and was then the tallest structure in the world.

title: Forth Bridge opens in Scotland
description: The Forth Bridge, a cantilever railway bridge over the Firth of Forth near Edinburgh, was opened in 1890 by the Duke of Rothesay (later Edward VII) and remains in use today.

title: Channel Tunnel officially opened
description: The Channel Tunnel, a 50 km rail link between Folkestone in England and Coquelles near Calais, 38 km of it under the sea, was officially opened at a ceremony in Calais in 1994. The pin marks the English portal.

title: Hoover Dam dedicated by Franklin D. Roosevelt
description: President Franklin D. Roosevelt dedicated Hoover Dam on the Colorado River in Black Canyon, on the Nevada-Arizona border, in 1935; the dam was handed to the government in 1936.

title: Golden Gate Bridge opens to pedestrians
description: The Golden Gate Bridge, a suspension bridge spanning the strait between San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean, opened in 1937 and was then the longest suspension bridge main span in the world.

title: Burj Khalifa opens in Dubai
description: Burj Khalifa in Dubai opened in 2010 as the tallest building in the world at 828 metres, a height it has kept since.

title: Home Insurance Building completed in Chicago
description: The Home Insurance Building in Chicago, completed in 1885 and demolished in 1931, is often cited as the first skyscraper, using a metal frame to carry much of its load.

title: Empire State Building opens in New York
description: The Empire State Building on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan opened in 1931 and was the tallest building in the world until 1970.

title: Sydney Harbour Bridge officially opened
description: The Sydney Harbour Bridge, a steel through-arch bridge linking the central business district with the North Shore, was officially opened in 1932.

title: Thames Tunnel opens between Rotherhithe and Wapping
description: The Thames Tunnel, built by Marc and Isambard Kingdom Brunel, opened in 1843 beneath the River Thames in London between Rotherhithe and Wapping.

title: First powered flight at Kitty Hawk
description: Orville Wright made the first sustained, controlled, powered heavier-than-air flight in the Wright Flyer near Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina, covering 120 feet.

title: Santos-Dumont flies the 14-bis at Bagatelle
description: Alberto Santos-Dumont flew the 14-bis about 220 metres at Bagatelle, winning the first officially observed record for a powered aeroplane flight in Europe.

title: Lindbergh lands at Le Bourget
description: Charles Lindbergh landed the Spirit of St. Louis at Le Bourget near Paris after 33.5 hours, completing the first solo non-stop transatlantic flight.

title: Stockton and Darlington Railway opens
description: The Stockton and Darlington Railway opened as the first public railway to use steam locomotives; Locomotion No. 1 hauled the first train over Skerne Bridge at Darlington.

title: Shanghai maglev opens for service
description: The Shanghai Maglev line, running from Longyang Road station to Pudong airport, opened as the first commercial high-speed magnetic levitation line in the world.

title: Tokaido Shinkansen opens in Tokyo
description: The Tokaido Shinkansen opened between Tokyo and Osaka, just before the Tokyo Olympics, as the world's first high-speed rail line.

title: First container ship voyage leaves Newark
description: Malcom McLean's converted tanker Ideal X sailed from Port Newark carrying 58 shipping containers, the first voyage of containerised cargo shipping.

title: Rainhill Trials won by Stephenson's Rocket
description: A locomotive competition held at Rainhill for the Liverpool and Manchester Railway, won by George and Robert Stephenson's Rocket. Coordinates are for Rainhill; the course lay east of the village.

title: Concorde makes its first flight at Toulouse
description: The first Concorde prototype, 001, made its maiden flight from Toulouse-Blagnac, starting the supersonic airliner's test programme.

title: Blériot flies across the English Channel
description: Louis Blériot flew his Blériot XI from near Calais to Dover in about 36 minutes, the first aeroplane crossing of the English Channel; the Blériot Memorial marks the landing.

title: Britain's first jet aircraft flies at Cranwell
description: The Gloster E.28/39, powered by Frank Whittle's turbojet, made its first flight from RAF Cranwell, the first flight of a British jet-powered aircraft.

title: Trevithick's locomotive runs at Penydarren
description: Richard Trevithick's steam locomotive hauled a load of iron and passengers along the Penydarren Tramroad from the ironworks, the first run of a railway steam locomotive.

title: Tennis for Two shown at Brookhaven Lab
description: William Higinbotham's oscilloscope tennis game was first shown at Brookhaven National Laboratory's public visitors' day in Upton, New York.

title: Spacewar! written at MIT's Building 26
description: MIT students programmed the space-combat game Spacewar! on a DEC PDP-1 in Building 26; it was first shown at the MIT Science Open House at the end of April 1962.

title: Pong prototype installed at Andy Capp's Tavern
description: Nolan Bushnell and Al Alcorn installed the Pong prototype in Andy Capp's Tavern in Sunnyvale, California, where it drew crowds and soon broke down from overflowing coins.

title: Tetris created at the Dorodnitsyn Computing Centre
description: Alexey Pajitnov, working at the Dorodnitsyn Computing Centre of the Academy of Sciences in Moscow, wrote the first version of Tetris in about three weeks.

title: HP Garage: Hewlett and Packard form a partnership
description: Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard formed their partnership in 1939 and built the HP 200A audio oscillator in a garage at 367 Addison Avenue, Palo Alto.

title: Doom shareware uploaded to a university FTP server
description: At midnight id Software uploaded the first episode of Doom to the University of Wisconsin-Madison FTP server, which was swamped by users trying to download it.

title: MUD1 created at the University of Essex
description: Roy Trubshaw and Richard Bartle created MUD, the first multi-user dungeon, on a DEC PDP-10 at the University of Essex, a forerunner of online virtual worlds.

title: Red Annihilation Quake tournament at E3
description: Held on the floor of E3 at the World Congress Center in Atlanta, the Quake tournament was won by Dennis 'Thresh' Fong, who took a Ferrari; it is seen as an early esports landmark.

title: OXO noughts-and-crosses game on EDSAC at Cambridge
description: Doctoral student Sandy Douglas wrote OXO, a noughts-and-crosses game, for the EDSAC computer at the University of Cambridge Mathematical Laboratory in 1952.

title: Bertie the Brain plays tic-tac-toe in Toronto
description: Josef Kates's Bertie the Brain, a tic-tac-toe machine, was exhibited at the Canadian National Exhibition in Toronto from 25 August to 9 September 1950.

title: Atari cartridges buried in Alamogordo landfill
description: Truckloads of unsold Atari cartridges and consoles were dumped and covered with concrete at the Alamogordo, New Mexico landfill, later estimated at about 700,000 cartridges.

title: Computer Space tested at the Dutch Goose bar
description: The first coin-operated video game, Computer Space, had its location test at the Dutch Goose bar in Menlo Park, California, near Stanford University.

title: Nimrod computer plays Nim at the Festival of Britain
description: The Nimrod computer, built by Ferranti to play the game of Nim, was first exhibited on 5 May 1951 at the Festival of Britain. The article does not name the venue, so the pin (South Kensington) is approximate.

title: The WELL online community launched in Sausalito
description: Stewart Brand and Larry Brilliant launched The WELL, an early online community whose offices were on Gate Five Road in Sausalito, California.

title: NORSAR links Norway to ARPANET
description: The NORSAR seismic array centre at Kjeller became the first non-US site on ARPANET in June 1973, linked via Tanum earth station in Sweden. In July the link reached University College London.

title: TAT-1 transatlantic telephone cable opens
description: TAT-1, the first transatlantic telephone cable, was inaugurated on 25 September 1956. Its UK end came ashore at Gallanach Bay near Oban, with Clarenville, Newfoundland, as the Canadian end.

title: TAT-8 first transatlantic fibre-optic cable
description: TAT-8, built in 1988, was the first transatlantic cable to use optical fibres. Its landing points were Tuckerton in New Jersey, Widemouth Bay in England and Penmarch in France.

title: First network email sent at BBN
description: Ray Tomlinson of Bolt, Beranek and Newman sent the first test email between two computers placed side by side in 1971, choosing the @ sign to separate user and host.

title: CYCLADES packet network first demonstrated
description: Louis Pouzin's CYCLADES network, sponsored by the French research agency IRIA, gave its first demonstration in November 1973 with three hosts and one packet switch.

title: NPL network packet switching goes live
description: The NPL network, designed by Donald Davies, became operational in early 1969 and was fully operational by January 1970, one of the first two packet-switched networks.

title: Metcalfe's memo outlines Ethernet
description: Robert Metcalfe wrote a 12-page memo at Xerox PARC on 22 May 1973 naming the concept 'The Ether Network', the basis of Ethernet local networking.

title: NCSA Mosaic alpha released
description: Marc Andreessen announced the first alpha version of NCSA Mosaic on 23 January 1993. The graphical web browser was developed at the National Center for Supercomputing Applications.

title: Archie, first Internet search tool, at McGill
description: Alan Emtage created Archie, an index of public FTP archive listings, at McGill University's School of Computer Science in Montreal; the article dates its release to 1990.

title: symbolics.com, first .com domain, registered
description: Symbolics, a Cambridge, Massachusetts computer maker, registered symbolics.com on 15 March 1985, the first .com domain name ever registered.

title: Google incorporated in a Menlo Park garage
description: Larry Page and Sergey Brin formally incorporated Google on 4 September 1998 in Susan Wojcicki's garage in Menlo Park, California.

title: Usenet established at Duke and UNC
description: Duke graduate students Tom Truscott and Jim Ellis conceived Usenet in 1979 and established it in 1980, first linking Duke with the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

title: Euler solves the Königsberg bridge problem
description: Euler presented his solution to the St Petersburg Academy on 26 August 1735. The problem concerned the seven bridges over the Pregel around Kneiphof island, where the pin is.

title: Hilbert presents his problems in Paris
description: At the International Congress of Mathematicians at the Sorbonne, David Hilbert presented ten of his 23 problems that shaped twentieth-century mathematics.

title: Goedel hints at incompleteness in Koenigsberg
description: At a conference in Königsberg Kurt Gödel made an off-hand remark in the final-day discussion that first announced his incompleteness theorems.

title: Ramanujan elected Fellow of Trinity College
description: Srinivasa Ramanujan was elected a Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge, the first Indian to receive that honour; he had come to Cambridge in 1914.

title: Wiles announces Fermat's Last Theorem proof
description: Andrew Wiles lectured at the Isaac Newton Institute in Cambridge on modular forms, elliptic curves and Galois representations, announcing a proof of Fermat's Last Theorem.

title: Bourbaki group first meets at Cafe Capoulade
description: The first unofficial meeting of the Bourbaki mathematicians took place at noon at the Café Grill-Room A. Capoulade in Paris's Latin Quarter.

title: Four colour theorem proved by computer at Illinois
description: Kenneth Appel and Wolfgang Haken announced a computer-assisted proof of the four colour theorem at the University of Illinois.

title: Hamilton carves the quaternion formula at Broom Bridge
description: William Rowan Hamilton discovered the fundamental formula of quaternion multiplication while walking and scratched it into a stone of Broom Bridge in Dublin.

title: Last problem written in the Scottish Book at Lwow
description: Mathematicians of the Lwów school wrote open problems in the Scottish Book at the Scottish Café; Hugo Steinhaus entered the final problem on this date.

title: Lobachevsky first reports non-Euclidean geometry at Kazan
description: Nikolai Lobachevsky first reported his new geometry, later called non-Euclidean, to a session of the physics and mathematics department at Kazan University.

title: Riemann gives his habilitation lecture at Goettingen
description: Bernhard Riemann delivered his lecture at Göttingen on the hypotheses underlying geometry, founding what became Riemannian geometry.

title: Turing elected Fellow of King's College Cambridge
description: Alan Turing was elected a Fellow of King's College, Cambridge, on the strength of his dissertation; he delivered his paper On Computable Numbers on 28 May 1936.

title: Transatlantic cable brought ashore at Heart's Content
description: The SS Great Eastern brought the 1866 transatlantic telegraph cable ashore at Heart's Content, Newfoundland, starting a lasting cable link to Europe. The station closed in 1965.

title: Marconi receives first transatlantic radio signal
description: Guglielmo Marconi reported receiving a transatlantic wireless signal from Cornwall at Signal Hill, St. John's, using a kite-borne aerial. He received it in a former fever hospital on the hill.

title: Niepce takes the oldest surviving photograph
description: Nicephore Niepce exposed the heliographic plate showing the view from his estate Le Gras at Saint-Loup-de-Varennes. It is the oldest surviving camera photograph; once dated 1826, the article now gives 1827.

title: Roundhay Garden Scene is filmed in Leeds
description: Louis Le Prince filmed the Whitley family in the garden of Oakwood Grange, Roundhay, Leeds. It is the oldest surviving motion picture, with a few seconds of footage.

title: BBC begins regular high-definition television
description: The BBC began what the article calls the world's first public high-definition television broadcasts from Alexandra Palace in north London in November 1936.

title: Morse's "What hath God wrought" received in Baltimore
description: Samuel Morse's first long-distance telegraph message, 'What hath God wrought', was sent from Washington on 24 May 1844 and received at the Mount Clare site of the B&O Railroad in Baltimore.

title: Andover station communicates with Telstar
description: AT&T's Andover ground station in Maine became operational in spring 1962 and served Telstar, the communications satellite launched from Cape Canaveral on 10 July 1962.

title: Fessenden's reported Christmas Eve radio broadcast
description: Reginald Fessenden reportedly broadcast music and speech from his 420 ft tower at Brant Rock, heard by ships. The date comes from his later letter; no independent proof has been found.

title: Cooke and Wheatstone demonstrate telegraph at Euston
description: A four-needle electric telegraph by William Cooke and Charles Wheatstone was successfully demonstrated between Euston and Camden Town in London. Coordinates are those of Euston station.

title: Baird demonstrates television at 22 Frith Street
description: John Logie Baird demonstrated television to members of the Royal Institution at 22 Frith Street in Soho, London, where he lived from 1924 to 1926. Coordinates are those of the street.

title: Lumiere brothers' first paid film screening in Paris
description: The Lumiere brothers held their first paid public film screening in the Salon Indien of the Grand Cafe in Paris, an early commercial showing of projected motion pictures.

title: Edison's Black Maria film studio opens
description: Thomas Edison's Black Maria in West Orange, New Jersey, the first film production studio, was finished in 1893. Early shorts such as Blacksmith Scene were made there that year.

title: First IVF baby born at Oldham
description: Louise Brown, the first baby born after in vitro fertilisation, was born at Oldham General Hospital, now the Royal Oldham Hospital, after treatment by Edwards and Steptoe.

title: Lister's first antiseptic success, Glasgow
description: At the Glasgow Royal Infirmary Lister treated 11-year-old James Greenlees's compound leg fracture with carbolic acid, his first success with antiseptic surgery.

title: Röntgen discovers X-rays in Würzburg
description: Working in his laboratory at the Physical Institute of the University of Würzburg, Röntgen observed a new kind of radiation, later called X-rays, on 8 November 1895.

title: First CT scan of a patient
description: At Atkinson Morley's Hospital in Wimbledon the first patient was scanned with Godfrey Hounsfield's EMI computed tomography prototype on 1 October 1971.

title: First successful kidney transplant, Boston
description: Surgeons at the Peter Bent Brigham Hospital transplanted a kidney between identical twins in 1954, the first successful kidney transplant; Joseph Murray later won a Nobel Prize.

title: Salk polio vaccine first tested at Arsenal school
description: Pittsburgh's Arsenal Elementary School hosted the first large-scale test of Jonas Salk's experimental polio vaccine in 1954, vaccinating about 135 pupils in grades one to three.

title: Super-Kamiokande finds neutrino oscillation evidence
description: The underground Super-Kamiokande detector in Japan, running since April 1996, announced the first strong evidence that muon neutrinos change into other neutrinos.

title: RHIC starts colliding heavy ions at Brookhaven
description: Brookhaven's Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider began operation in 2000 and went on to study quark-gluon plasma by colliding heavy ions.

title: Dounreay Fast Reactor feeds the National Grid
description: Dounreay's experimental fast breeder reactor, first critical in 1959, began supplying power to the National Grid on the north coast of Scotland.

title: OPERA announces apparent faster-than-light neutrinos
description: OPERA, an underground detector at Gran Sasso, announced neutrinos sent from CERN apparently travelled faster than light; the result was later traced to errors.

title: November Revolution: J/psi found at SLAC
description: Teams at SLAC and Brookhaven announced the J/psi particle, evidence of the charm quark; the SLAC team used the SPEAR collider.

title: Submarine prototype reactor goes critical in Idaho
description: The land-based prototype of the Nautilus reactor first went critical at the Naval Reactors Facility in Idaho and ran a simulated Atlantic crossing that May.

title: Michelson and Morley test for the luminiferous ether
description: Albert Michelson and Edward Morley used an interferometer in the basement of Adelbert dormitory at Western Reserve University, Cleveland, and found no ether wind.

title: Millikan's oil-drop experiment measures the electron charge
description: At the University of Chicago, Robert Millikan and Harvey Fletcher measured the elementary electric charge by balancing charged oil droplets between electrified plates.

title: Foucault shows Earth's rotation with a pendulum
description: Léon Foucault hung a 67-metre pendulum from the dome of the Panthéon in Paris, whose slowly turning swing plane showed Earth's rotation to the public.

title: Davisson and Germer diffract electrons at Bell Labs
description: At Bell Telephone Laboratories in New York, Clinton Davisson and Lester Germer scattered electrons off a nickel crystal and observed diffraction, confirming wave behaviour of matter.

title: Eddington's eclipse expedition tests general relativity
description: During a total solar eclipse, Arthur Eddington's team at Roça Sundy on Príncipe photographed stars near the Sun to measure light deflection predicted by general relativity.

title: Kamerlingh Onnes discovers superconductivity at Leiden
description: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes and his team at Leiden University found that the electrical resistance of mercury vanished when cooled to a few kelvin with liquid helium.

title: First Bose–Einstein condensate created at JILA
description: Eric Cornell and Carl Wieman at JILA in Boulder cooled rubidium-87 atoms to nanokelvin temperatures and produced the first gaseous Bose–Einstein condensate.

title: Maiman operates the first laser at Hughes Research Labs
description: Theodore Maiman fired the first working laser, a pulsed ruby device, at the Hughes Research Laboratories on the Malibu hillside in California.

title: Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction
description: Michael Faraday at the Royal Institution in London showed that a changing magnetic field induces an electric current in a nearby coil of wire.

title: Stern and Gerlach observe quantised spin in Frankfurt
description: Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach sent silver atoms through an inhomogeneous magnetic field and saw the beam split in two, showing quantised angular momentum.

title: Pound and Rebka measure gravitational redshift at Harvard
description: Robert Pound and Glen Rebka measured the gravitational redshift of gamma rays over the 22.5-metre tower of Harvard's Jefferson Laboratory, as predicted by general relativity.

title: Isolation of graphene at the University of Manchester
description: Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov at the University of Manchester isolated single-atom-thick graphene flakes from graphite using adhesive tape.

title: Franklin expedition winters on Beechey Island
description: Franklin chose the sheltered harbour of Beechey Island for his first winter camp. Three crewmen buried there were found by searchers in 1850.

title: Shackleton's hut at Cape Royds
description: Shackleton's British Antarctic Expedition built its hut at Cape Royds in 1908, and the party wintered there during the 1907–09 expedition.

title: First station built at the South Pole
description: US Navy Seabees built the first station at the geographic South Pole from November 1956. A party of 18 men under Paul Siple wintered there for the IGY.

title: Alert weather station established
description: Twelve personnel arrived to set up Alert, the last of five Joint Arctic Weather Stations built by Canada and the United States, on Ellesmere Island.

title: Svalbard Global Seed Vault opens
description: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault officially opened on 26 February 2008 near Longyearbyen as a secure backup store for crop seed samples.

title: Soviet drift station North Pole-1 set up
description: The first Soviet drifting ice station was established on 21 May 1937 about 20 km from the North Pole, and was evacuated on 19 February 1938.

title: Polish codebreakers break Enigma in Warsaw
description: Polish Cipher Bureau cryptologists, working in the Saxon Palace, first broke the German Enigma cipher in December 1932.

title: First British Bombe installed at Bletchley Park
description: The first British Bombe, Victory, was installed in Hut 1 at Bletchley Park to speed the breaking of Enigma keys.

title: DES published as US federal standard
description: The National Bureau of Standards published DES as FIPS PUB 46, authorised for unclassified government data.

title: RSA public-key cipher devised at MIT
description: Rivest, Shamir and Adleman devised the RSA public-key cryptosystem at MIT; Rivest drafted the paper overnight after a Passover gathering.

title: Room 40 decodes the Zimmermann Telegram
description: British naval codebreakers in the Admiralty partly decoded Germany's secret offer of an alliance to Mexico, helping bring the US into the war.

title: Venona codebreaking begins at Arlington Hall
description: The US Army's Signal Intelligence Service began the Venona project at Arlington Hall to read Soviet diplomatic and intelligence cables.

title: Kryptos sculpture dedicated at CIA headquarters
description: Jim Sanborn's Kryptos, a copper sculpture carrying four encrypted messages, was dedicated in the courtyard of CIA headquarters; part of it remains unsolved.

title: Stuxnet worm targets Iran's Natanz plant
description: Stuxnet, a worm aimed at industrial controllers at the Natanz enrichment facility, was first publicly identified in June 2010.

title: Stoll traces a hacker at Berkeley Lab
description: While running computers at Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory, Clifford Stoll investigated a persistent intruder, an episode he later recounted in a book.

title: Sony Pictures hack paralyses Culver City studio
description: Malware disabled many Sony Pictures employee computers and leaked internal data; the company is based in Culver City.

title: Morris worm released from MIT's network
description: Robert Tappan Morris launched the first widely spread internet worm at 8:30 pm, routing it via MIT's network.

title: Room 40 codebreaking unit formed at the Admiralty
description: Britain's naval codebreaking group Room 40 formed in October 1914 and occupied rooms in the Admiralty Old Building, Whitehall.

title: Diffie and Hellman publish key exchange
description: Whitfield Diffie and Martin Hellman, working at Stanford, published New Directions in Cryptography, introducing public key exchange.

title: Navajo code talkers recruited and trained
description: Twenty-nine Navajo recruits were sworn in on 4 May 1942 and, at Camp Pendleton, created the Navajo code for the US Marines.

title: First BASIC program runs at Dartmouth
description: John Kemeny and John McGeachie ran the first BASIC program at 4 a.m. on 1 May 1964 on Dartmouth's time-sharing system, which was housed in College Hall.

title: Smalltalk interpreter written at Xerox PARC
description: At Xerox PARC, Dan Ingalls wrote the first Smalltalk interpreter in October 1972, after a bet by Alan Kay; it was ported to the Xerox Alto in April 1973.

title: Unix development begins at Bell Labs
description: Ken Thompson, Dennis Ritchie and colleagues began developing Unix at the Bell Labs research center in 1969; the first internal manual followed in November 1971.

title: Dennis Ritchie creates C at Bell Labs
description: Dennis Ritchie developed the C programming language at Bell Labs between 1972 and 1973 as a successor to B; Unix version 4 was rewritten in C in 1973.

title: Stallman announces the GNU Project
description: Richard Stallman announced the GNU Project on 27 September 1983, a plan for a free Unix-compatible system; he had worked at the MIT AI Lab, then at 545 Technology Square.

title: Torvalds announces Linux on comp.os.minix
description: While studying at the University of Helsinki, Linus Torvalds announced his free operating system project on comp.os.minix on 25 August 1991; kernel 0.01 followed on 17 September.

title: Python implementation begins at CWI
description: Guido van Rossum began implementing Python in December 1989 at the CWI research institute in the Netherlands; he published version 0.9.1 on alt.sources in February 1991.

title: ALGOL 58 designed at ETH Zurich
description: ACM and GAMM delegates met at ETH Zurich from 27 May to 2 June 1958 to merge their proposals into a universal algorithmic language, which became ALGOL 58.

title: Pentagon meeting launches COBOL
description: A meeting held at the Pentagon on 28-29 May 1959 and chaired by Charles Phillips began work on a common business programming language; CODASYL was named on 4 June.

title: Netscape announces free browser source code
description: On 22 January 1998 Netscape announced its browser would be free, and soon released its source code, starting the open-source Mozilla project; it was based in Mountain View.

title: JavaScript released in Netscape Navigator
description: Brendan Eich created JavaScript at Netscape, first shipped as LiveScript in a Navigator beta in September 1995 and renamed JavaScript for the December 1995 release.

title: Apple founded at the Jobs home in Los Altos
description: On 1 April 1976 Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne founded Apple; operations started at the Jobs family home on Crist Drive in Los Altos, California.

title: CTSS first demonstrated at MIT
description: Fernando Corbato's Compatible Time-Sharing System was first demonstrated on MIT's modified IBM 709 in November 1961, one of the first time-sharing systems.

title: Pascal compiler becomes operational in Zurich
description: Niklaus Wirth released Pascal in 1970; its first compiler, written in Zurich for the CDC 6000 series, was operational by mid-1970.
